Subject: POC kickoff: hands-on prompt review + routing & load testing

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Acme is excited to run a short POC to validate routing, prompt behavior across our SKU catalog, and a couple of lightweight load tests. We'd like the POC to be hands-on so our engineers can iterate on prompts with you in real time.

High level asks:
- 90-minute kickoff + hands-on workshop (prompt inventory + guardrails + structured output)
- One 20-minute window reserved for a brief load test (burst at ~10-20 qps) to validate cost/latency
- A shared prompt inventory template so we can populate prompts beforehand

Can you propose 2x time slots this week or early next? Also let us know whether Redwood needs a dedicated test environment or if we can run load tests in your hosted sandbox.

Attaching our current feature list for the scope.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Head of ML Platforms
Acme Retail

Hi Samantha — great to hear, and glad the demo landed well.

Proposed slots (Pacific time):
- Wed 20 May, 09:30–11:00 PT
- Thu 21 May, 13:00–14:30 PT

Suggested agenda (attached: Redwood_POC_Agenda_v2.pdf and prompt_inventory_template.csv):
1) 10m — Introductions & success criteria
2) 30m — Prompt inventory walkthrough (we'll ask you to share a few representative prompts)
3) 30m — Hands-on prompt tuning + structured output examples (JSON schema, field-level constraints)
4) 20m — Routing & fallback discussion (how to route by latency/cost/region)
5) 20m — Load test window — 2x 10-minute bursts with monitoring (we'll define QPS/seq length)
6) 10m — Mutual action items & next steps

Notes:
- For the load test, our recommended approach is to use a dedicated test pool (Redwood Dedicated sandbox) so results don't interfere with other tenants. If ACME prefers hosted sandbox, we'll need to limit concurrency to avoid noise.
- Please pre-fill the prompt inventory sheet for the prompts you care most about (we'll focus on 6–8 prompts during the workshop).

I included Karthik (inference lead) to confirm the test environment and Marissa on scheduling/logistics.

If either of those slots works, we'll lock it and send a calendar invite + Zoom link and a short mutual action plan.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: POC kickoff: hands-on prompt review + routing & load testing

Thanks Vanessa. A couple operational clarifications from the infra side:

- Recommended: run load tests in a short, isolated Dedicated sandbox. I can stand up a 1-node pool with the quantization profile we'll use for latency baselines.
- Load test plan: two bursts at 15 qps for 10 minutes each, payloads with 256-token generation target. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost.
- We'll need ACME to share a small sample of the prompt set (anonymized OK) so the KV cache behavior is realistic.

If ACME prefers not to use Dedicated, we can do a constrained run in hosted sandbox but you'll likely see latency variance — fine for functional tests but not for tight SLA modeling.

I'll add Sergio (CS lead) for the mutual action plan and to coordinate access.

On availability: Wed 20 May 09:30 PT works for me.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Inference
Redwood Inference
